commits.edited_message:
Reject an XML declaration version other than "1.[0-9]+"

Fixes GH-967 (the version-string half of it; the URI-validation half
is a separate, bigger topic already discussed on the issue).

doParseXmlDecl in xmltok.c never actually validated the version
pseudo-attribute's value beyond checking it's non-empty and made of
the usual pseudo-attribute-value characters. So a document like

  <?xml version="2.3"?>
  <root/>

parsed just fine, even though Expat only implements XML 1.0 Fourth
Edition and section 2.8 of the spec says a processor should reject a
document declaring a version it doesn't support.

Adds checkXmlDeclVersionNum(), which checks the version value against
XML 1.0 Fifth Edition's relaxed VersionNum production ("1." followed
by one or more digits) rather than the stricter Fourth Edition literal
"1.0". Fifth Edition versions like "1.1" are accepted (Expat itself
still only implements 1.0's semantics) so that support isn't rejected
now only to be un-rejected once Expat tracks the Fifth Edition later;
anything outside that pattern falls through to the existing bad-value
path and surfaces as XML_ERROR_XML_DECL, same as an empty version
already does.

Adds test_xmldecl_wrong_version_number and
test_xmldecl_accepts_1_x_version covering both the rejected and
accepted cases. Ran the full test suite under a plain debug build and
again under ASan+UBSan, both 100% green (4908 checks). Ran clang-format
23 over both changed files with no diff.

Also reject a single-byte EncName that does not fit in a 128-byte
working copy. XML_ENC_NAME_MAX is 127 name bytes so the NUL still fits;
names that fit are copied and checked against the EncName production
before the encoding is resolved, and names that do not fit surface as
XML_ERROR_XML_DECL.

lib: reject UTF-16 high surrogate not followed by a low surrogate

Raise the encoding-name scratch limit to 128 bytes. findEncoding sizes
its buffer from XML_ENC_NAME_MAX and keeps the extra byte for the
terminator, so a 128-byte EncName converts and is looked up instead of
being rejected for length.

coupling: db49508 copies a single-byte EncName into a fixed 128-byte stack buffer and treats XML_ENC_NAME_MAX as the maximum number of name bytes, not counting the NUL. When that macro is unset the commit defines it as 127, so the longest name it copies is 127 bytes and encName[nlen] = '\0' stays inside the array; a 128-byte name is rejected before the copy. 768a1ce sets XML_ENC_NAME_MAX to 128 and sizes findEncoding's scratch buffer as XML_ENC_NAME_MAX + 1, so the bytes that converter writes, including the NUL, stay inside its own buffer. Each diff is consistent with the contract it states: the declaration parser is safe at the 127-byte default, and findEncoding is safe at the new 128-byte limit. The overflow exists only in the composition, where the declaration parser still allocates char encName[128] but the shared limit now permits nlen == 128 and the terminator is stored one past that array. A fix has to reconcile those two sites; adjusting only findEncoding's buffer, or only the 127 default inside the declaration parser, leaves the other commit's contract unchanged and the disagreement in place.
